_comment: Hand-curated metadata merged with upstream.json by scripts/build_registry.py. Values here are curated claims, NOT upstream-verified: the build records binary_source=curated unless crates.io/Cargo.toml confirm the binary. 'unknown' means not established. Flags marked (vd) are version-dependent: the harness checks `--help` before relying on them.

fd.input: pattern (regex by default, --glob for globs) + optional paths
fd.output: one path per line; -0 for NUL-separated
fd.exit: 0 on success even with zero matches; with -q exit 1 means no match; 1 on error
limitations: Respects .gitignore and skips hidden files by default — use -u to match find semantics
Regex by default, not glob
Interactive only; use ripgrep for automation
Long-running server, not a one-shot CLI; set a master key outside development

qdrant-es-gateway.notes: Recently added gateway; binary name and install method not established.

limitations: Interactive; writes files after confirmation in the UI

flags.--files: list files that would be searched

ripgrep.exit: 0 = match found, 1 = no match, 2 = error (2 can coexist with matches)
limitations: Respects .gitignore and skips hidden/binary files by default
Rust regex: no backreferences/lookaround unless -P (PCRE2 build)
Needs a TTY; pipe selection into the next step only when a human is present
Windows support limited

reflex.notes: Trigram index + MCP server per README; binary name not established — check upstream before use.
limitations: Requires building an index before queries

diskus.output: single human-readable total, e.g. '1.25 GB (1,251,234,567 bytes)'

flags.-b / --apparent-size: apparent size instead of disk usage

limitations: Only a total — no breakdown

broot.notes: The 'br' shell function wrapper is installed via `broot --install`.

limitations: Human-oriented output; terminal width affects layout

fselect.input: SQL-like query: select path, size from DIR where size gt 1M order by size desc limit 20

dependencies: ZFS/btrfs/nilfs2 snapshots, Time Machine or Restic

lscolors.notes: Primarily a library; CLI colorizes paths read from args/stdin.

flags.-s: seance: list buried files in cwd

limitations: Graveyard defaults to /tmp on some setups — may not survive reboot
Upstream is little maintained; the rip2 fork continues it
macOS not supported for list/restore
`trash empty` is irreversible
Ranks from the user's history — results are not reproducible across machines

bat.output: highlighted text; acts like cat when piped

limitations: Binary name hx collides with helix's hx

flags.-y / -n: assume yes / no to overwrite prompts

limitations: Prompts on overwrite unless -y/-n given — always pass one in automation
Some formats (rar) decompress-only

flags.(default): dry run — shows changes, writes nothing

limitations: Respects .gitignore like ripgrep
Not a drop-in for every cp flag
Passive observation only; runs until killed — wrap with timeout
No non-interactive snapshot mode; use procs/ps/free/vmstat for evidence
Active scanning — authorized networks only
Pager may engage on TTY; use --pager disable (vd)
Active scanning — authorized targets only
An open port list is not a security assessment

dependencies: root or CAP_NET_RAW (unprivileged mode on some platforms)

limitations: Personal shell history may contain secrets — read only when the user asks

just.exit: propagates the failing recipe line's exit code

limitations: TUI — for agent automation prefer rust-parallel or background jobs with captured logs
mprocs.notes: Upstream renamed to dekit (pvolok/dekit); current HEAD builds only `dekit`. Older mprocs 0.9.x releases install an `mprocs` binary (kept as alias).

limitations: Writes files in place without backup when given paths — preview with -p first
Regex syntax differs from sed (Rust regex, $1 captures)

shrs.notes: Rust crate for building shells, not a ready CLI.

starship.notes: Prompt renderer; not useful as an agent tool beyond `starship explain`.

hyperfine.exit: non-zero if a benchmarked command fails (unless -i)
limitations: Measures wall-clock of whole commands; noisy on busy machines — compare with same settings

inferno.input: perf script / dtrace output or folded stacks on stdin

dependencies: ptrace permission or root for attaching to other processes

install: build from source (cargo build --release -p bytehound-preload / -p bytehound-cli)
dependencies: yarn/nodejs for the web UI build

delta.input: unified diff on stdin (or two files)
limitations: Presentation-only: output is for humans; agents should read raw `git diff`
Falls back to line diff for unsupported languages or very large files
Not a patch format — cannot be applied
Passive; runs until killed — wrap with timeout

forge.notes: AI pair programmer (antinomyhq/forge, a.k.a. forgecode); install method varies by release — consult upstream.

flags.git absorb: create fixup! commits for staged changes

limitations: Requires authorization: creates commits, and --and-rebase rewrites history
CLI is a dev tool; plumbing coverage is partial vs git — prefer git for correctness

gity.notes: fsmonitor daemon; affects git behavior repo-wide once enabled.

limitations: Generated regex matches the examples; it does not generalize semantically — test it

hurl.exit: 0 ok, 1 CLI/options error, 2 input parse error, 3 runtime error, 4 assert failure

jaq.input: JSON (and YAML/CBOR/TOML/XML in newer versions, vd) on stdin or files
jaq.exit: 0 ok; non-zero on parse or filter error
limitations: Mostly but not fully jq-compatible (e.g. some builtins, path semantics)
Only use in repos the user already manages with jj; colocating jj with git changes repo state

install: prebuilt binaries from GitHub releases (qsv, qsvlite, qsvdp variants)
limitations: Feature set differs by build variant — check `qsv --list`

rust-sqlite.notes: Educational SQLite-like database; not a sqlite3 replacement.

limitations: Binary name tldr collides with tlrc and the Node tldr client
Binary name tldr collides with tealdeer

flags.-o json: JSON output (needs a build with output formats; vd)

limitations: Upstream recommends qsv/xan as maintained successors
hx collides with the hex tool's binary
Not 100% GNU-compatible for every flag; check behaviour for edge cases

flags.'EXPR': evaluate once, e.g. fend '5 GiB to MB'

limitations: Accesses the user's mailbox — only with explicit request

ratatui.notes: Rust crate for building TUIs; no binary.

limitations: Never start without explicit user request
Never invoke autonomously; privilege escalation requires explicit user approval
